title: GraphQL vs REST
definition: Comparing the two dominant Web API architectures. REST relies on multiple endpoints returning fixed data structures. GraphQL relies on a single endpoint returning dynamic, client-defined data structures.
simpleExplanation: REST is a set menu at a restaurant. You order the 'Burger Meal' (Endpoint), and you get a burger, fries, and a drink, whether you want them or not. GraphQL is a buffet. You walk up to one counter (Single Endpoint) and put exactly 3 fries and half a burger on your plate.
realWorldExample: To show a blog dashboard, a REST app makes 3 requests: `/user`, `/posts`, and `/followers`. A GraphQL app makes 1 request to `/graphql` asking for the user, their posts, and their followers all at once.

basic: How many Endpoints (URLs) does a standard GraphQL API usually expose?
intermediate: Why is HTTP Caching inherently harder in GraphQL compared to REST?

answers.question: How many endpoints?
answers.answer: Usually just ONE (e.g., `POST /graphql`). All queries and mutations are sent to this single URL.

answers.question: Why is caching harder?
answers.answer: REST relies on unique URLs. Browsers and CDNs know how to easily cache `GET /users/5`. Because GraphQL sends almost every request as a `POST` to the exact same `/graphql` URL with a complex body, standard network caching breaks down. You have to use complex client-side caching libraries like Apollo.
